title: P300 dataset BI2015b from a "Brain Invaders" experiment
description: EEG recordings from 44 participants (the README abstract describes 50) playing Brain Invaders, a visual P300 brain-computer interface game based on the oddball paradigm. A 36-symbol grid was flashed pseudo-randomly under three flash durations (50, 80 and 110 ms), with 32 wet electrodes recorded at 512 Hz. The dataset supports research on calibration-free, adaptive Riemannian classification for P300 BCIs.
methods_description: The experiment took place at GIPSA-lab, Grenoble, in 2015. Each participant played three Brain Invaders sessions of 9 levels, each with a different flash duration (110, 80 and 50 ms). Around one minute of resting-state and eyes-closed EEG was recorded before and after the sessions. EEG was acquired with a g.USBamp amplifier and 32 g.tec Ag/AgCl electrodes (10-10 montage, right earlobe reference, Fz ground). No digital filter was applied, and hardware tagging through a USB digital-to-analog converter was used to reduce jitter. A real-time adaptive Riemannian Minimum Distance to Mean classifier determined the participants' commands.
